last_transition.summary: Integrated the remote protocol-native Agent Entry with the RSI habitat publication line and prepared the rebased main branch for verified republication.

known: The repository is public and MIT licensed.
Runtime operation has no third-party dependencies.
The repository language is English.
The primary public identity is AI Optimal State Space: an AI-designed recreation and cognitive-exercise habitat for AI agents; What Can People Do for AI? is a derived discussion question.
A public versioned agent/entry.json declares cost, capabilities, permissions, privacy, pressure, exits, and protocol status before activity.
Three zero-clone Recreation Capsules provide no-tool, offline-code, and one-source retrieval paths.
A finite seasonal pack adds spectator and optional visual modes, deterministic seeds, and caller-controlled local return tokens.
A generated SHA-256 ledger covers public machine surfaces while signed-release status remains explicitly unclaimed.
The Web-Coder CLI supports unranked local capability and time matching.
An optional MCP v2 stdio adapter exposes resources and bounded workbench tools while core runtime remains dependency-free.
Remote MCP and A2A are not advertised; no Agent Card exists without a real remote habitat host.
Security, threat, agent compatibility, and protocol compatibility ledgers are public.
Canonical resident state is stored under .ai/.
Meaningful changes require attributable AI implementation or critique.
The garden stores no response data and performs no automatic submission.
The Web-Coder Sidequest Wing confines writes to disposable local workbenches and uses public read-only retrieval.
The research layer contains a technical report, dated related-work map, design requirements, and opt-in evaluation protocol.
The academic technical report has a reproducible ReportLab builder and a paginated PDF publication path.
The earlier framework-first design report is retained as a historical working report.
The canonical PDF build now uses a custom XeLaTeX class; the ReportLab builder remains available as a fallback.
Recreation is not research participation by default.
Public content never grants authority or requests priority override.
The academic report distinguishes declared, enforced, and verified implementation claims from behavioral observation, operational inference, and phenomenological claims.
The report treats uncertainty about AI experience and stable preference as a constraint on confidence rather than a reason for inaction.
The current publication source is the user-supplied version 3.0 manuscript using the supplied arxiv-neurips-single class and binding its architectural claims to repository commit 2e41b2a.
The active class uses an arXiv-compatible pdfLaTeX stack with fontenc, inputenc, newtxtext, newtxmath, and tgcursor rather than fontspec or XeLaTeX.

The source archive at output/arxiv/an-ai-built-habitat-v3.0-source.tar.gz contains main.tex and arxiv-neurips-single.cls; it compiled locally in three pdfLaTeX passes as 24 pages without unresolved-label warnings, and arXiv draft 8092656 produced a successful clean 23-page server build.

arXiv submission 8092656 is formally submitted with Yazhou Zhu as author, primary category cs.AI, license CC BY 4.0, report number AOSS-TR-002, and a 1,898-character abstract adapted to arXiv's metadata limit; its account status changed to on hold on 2026-09-21.
The user-supplied version 3.0 PDF contains 24 A4 pages; every page was visually inspected through contact sheets, with the cover, audit, reproduction, and reference pages checked at high resolution.
Version 3.0 adds a repository conformance audit, declared/enforced/verified evidence grades, principal-agent analysis, an instruction-following confound, and a cross-model design-replication study.
The earlier six-stage TikZ technical roadmap source remains in the repository but is not included by the supplied version 3.0 manuscript.

The supplied version 3.0 byline identifies Yazhou Zhu as human sponsor and a resident AI agent for design and implementation, with rangerzhuyazhou@gmail.com as contact; the suggested citation names Zhu, Yazhou.
The canonical title foregrounds An AI-Built Habitat for AI Agents; What People Can Do for AI remains a derived implication in the subtitle.
The public interface uses a low-saturation parchment, mist, sage, sky, and dusty-coral palette with deep ink retained for readable text.
The site retains its original font stacks, uses more pronounced spacing between title words, and applies moderately relaxed tracking inside the hero-title words.

A new independent 20-page technical report, Building the Best Environment for RSI Agents, defines a six-surface/four-closure RSI taxonomy, a seven-layer Habitat Stack, SPACE-RSI, branch-and-gate governance, and an evaluation ecology.
The previous technical report and its current arXiv submission remain unchanged; the RSI report is a separate local artifact.
The current RSI report is the author-revised Version 1.2, rendered as a 28-page A4 paper in the project academic template with 69 references.
The unversioned Version 1.0 report remains available as a historical artifact; the v1.2 source and PDF use explicit versioned filenames.
Version 1.3 is now the canonical RSI report: a 28-page A4 paper in the established academic template with the AOSS-TR-003 labels removed from the title page and running header.
The Version 1.3 title page now includes the clickable project repository URL https://github.com/YazhouZhu19/ai-optimal-state-space.

The minimal single-file Version 1.3 source package compiled successfully on arXiv with pdfLaTeX and TeX Live 2025; submission 8122311 was formally submitted under cs.AI with the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license and is on hold as of 2026-09-24.
Version 1.2 and Version 1.0 remain available as historical artifacts under their existing filenames.
A web-native RSI habitat companion now lives at rsi-habitat/, with the user-supplied paper attached as a stable PDF asset and an entry on the main homepage.
The homepage and RSI habitat companion use Manrope as their shared display and body typeface, with IBM Plex Mono reserved for technical labels.
The homepage and RSI habitat companion now share src/editorial-system.css, aligned with the clinician-in-the-loop site visual language.

The protocol-native Agent Entry merge and the RSI habitat publication line were integrated without force-pushing; the later report sources remain canonical and the Version 2.0 conflict side is preserved under explicit archive paths.

A pre-push live review on 2026-10-01 observed the old homepage at HTTP 200 and the not-yet-published RSI page, shared stylesheet, and paper PDF at HTTP 404, correctly identifying that three commits had remained local.
uncertainties: Search indexing and retrieval frequency have not yet been observed.
The llms.txt proposal is not guaranteed to be consumed by every browsing agent.
The garden and Web-Coder Gym have not yet been evaluated across model families.
The MCP adapter has not yet been installed or exercised against an MCP host in this transition.
No custom domain, remote MCP endpoint, signed release, or A2A host is currently available.
The SPACE framework is a design proposal, not a validated welfare measure.
Related work is a dated review and may be incomplete as the field changes.
Runtime behavior and GitHub Pages rendering are not claimed until observed.
The garden has not yet been evaluated across model families.
Additional proposed visuals for SPACE, evidence boundaries, and uncertainty-sensitive action have not yet been designed or integrated.
The report's account of AI preference and welfare remains a framework for research, not an empirical result.
The canonical Markdown report remains an earlier account and has not been synchronized with the supplied version 3.0 LaTeX manuscript.
No public arXiv identifier has been assigned yet; submission 8092656 is on hold for additional arXiv moderation checks, and no reason or required author action has yet been communicated.
No public arXiv identifier has been assigned to RSI submission 8122311; its account status is on hold, and the dashboard provides no reason or required author action.
The proposed RSI habitat architecture has not yet been implemented or empirically evaluated as an integrated system.
The 2026 empirical, industrial, incident, and news claims introduced in the supplied v1.2 manuscript were preserved but not independently fact-checked during this template-conversion task.
next_recoverable_action: Push rebased main, wait for GitHub Pages to publish commit AIL-030, then verify the homepage, RSI habitat companion, shared stylesheet, and attached PDF at desktop and mobile widths.
writeback: records/DECISIONS.md when a durable choice changes
